Sending to Remotes

Source: vignettes/send-to-remotes.Rmd
send-to-remotes.Rmd

projr can automatically send artifacts to remote destinations during production builds (projr_build_patch(), projr_build_minor(), projr_build_major()). Development builds (projr_build_dev()) never upload to remotes.

Supported remote types:

  • GitHub Releases in the analysis repository or a specified destination repository
  • Local directories – local, network-mounted, or cloud-synced folders

Archive directories by their configured labels, such as raw-data, output, or docs. Select cache explicitly to include it. GitHub supplies its own source-code download for the commit at the release tag.

Put the address of a named archive under remotes and select it under build.dest. This example publishes documents to a GitHub release named reports in the analysis repository.

remotes:
  github:
    reports: {}
build:
  dest:
    reports:
      content: [docs]

To pause uploads, remove reports from build.dest. Readers can still get previously published reports with projr_get_github(remote = "reports", label = "docs") from a project where that name is registered. See the configuration reference for local archives, separate GitHub repositories, and the all-label selection. The helpers below write both the remotes entry and the build.dest selection.

GitHub Destinations

Configure a GitHub remote for the checkout and a credential with write access to releases in the destination repository. Run projr_instr_auth_github() for setup.

# Add a GitHub release for raw data
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "raw-data-@version",
  content = "raw-data"
)

# Add a GitHub release for outputs
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "output-@version",
  content = "output"
)

YAML equivalent:

remotes:
  github:
    "raw-data-@version": {}
    "output-@version": {}
build:
  dest:
    "raw-data-@version":
      content: [raw-data]
    "output-@version":
      content: [output]

Parameters:

  • title names the archive under remotes.github and sets both the release name and the Git tag. For version 1.2.3, "archive-@version" produces archive-v1.2.3. The literal "archive" shares one release across versions.
  • branch optionally sets the branch in the GitHub repository whose commit a newly created release should target. Use branch: "@branch" for the current checkout’s branch. A missing branch or a conflicting existing Git tag stops release creation.
  • content – directory label to archive (for example, raw-data or output).

Local Destinations

Choose a writable local or mounted folder. Relative paths resolve from the project root.

# Archive to local directory
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "local-backup",
  content = "output",
  path = "~/project-archive/output"
)

# Archive to network drive
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "network-backup",
  content = "raw-data",
  path = "/mnt/shared/projects/my-project/data"
)

YAML equivalent:

remotes:
  local:
    local-backup:
      path: "~/project-archive/output"
build:
  dest:
    local-backup:
      content: [output]

Parameters:

  • title – name of the archive under remotes.local.
  • content – directory label to archive.
  • path – destination directory (absolute or project-relative).

In YAML, path-append-label: false omits the label directory. An archive then stores files under <path>/v1.2.3/, while a latest destination stores them directly under <path>/. Both keep their directory histories in <path>/manifests/. A latest destination with this layout reserves the top-level names manifests, manifest.csv, VERSION, and CHANGELOG.md for release metadata. Files in subdirectories can use those names. For this latest layout, the destination’s VERSION and matching manifest record an empty build. When all archived files go missing after a populated build, projr_source(conflict = "remote") leaves the local files in place.

Local destination names and paths and GitHub release names accept @branch, @version, and @uuid. For example, archives/@branch/@version-@uuid keeps a separate local archive for each build. Find the concrete title and destination in the Resolved archive destinations section of .projr/BUILDLOG.md. Use projr_restore(version = "1.2.3") in a checkout to restore the inputs from a build published with archive_github = TRUE. To copy published directories elsewhere, use projr_get_local() or projr_get_github() with version and out. The restore guide covers both workflows.

Customization Options

Both GitHub and local remotes accept the same optional parameters. Defaults are shown first.

structure

How versions are organized on the remote.

Value Behaviour
"archive" (default) Keeps uploaded files under their build version. Unchanged files can be retrieved from a matching earlier upload.
"latest" Overwrites the same location each build

Use "archive" for reproducibility; "latest" for always-current snapshots.

send_cue

When to create a new version on the remote.

Value Behaviour
"if-change" (default) Upload only when content changed since last version
"always" Upload every build, even if unchanged

send_strategy

How files are transferred.

Value Behaviour
"sync-diff" (default) Upload changed/new files, remove deleted files
"sync-purge" Replace the files for the selected label at the destination
"upload-all" Upload all files (may overwrite)
"upload-missing" Upload only files not present on remote

Use "sync-diff" for efficiency. Use "sync-purge" to guarantee no stale files. Avoid "upload-missing" if you delete files locally.

send_inspect

How projr determines what already exists on the remote.

Value Behaviour
"manifest" (default) Read the remote manifest (fast)
"file" Download and hash actual remote files (slower, always accurate)
"none" Treat remote as empty (forces full upload)

Local archives keep their history in manifests/. A GitHub Release holds one manifest.zip. While an upload updates that ZIP, it claims projr-manifest.lock on the same release. If a second upload encounters the lock, retry it after the first upload finishes. If the first process was terminated, confirm that it has stopped before removing its lock asset.

Complete Configuration Examples

Comprehensive GitHub setup 

# Raw data: reuse the earlier upload on the same release when unchanged
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "raw-data",
  content = "raw-data",
  structure = "archive",
  send_cue = "if-change",
  send_strategy = "sync-diff",
  send_inspect = "manifest"
)

# Output: archive every version
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "output-@version",
  content = "output",
  structure = "archive",
  send_cue = "always",
  send_strategy = "sync-diff",
  send_inspect = "manifest"
)

# Docs: overwrite with latest
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "docs-latest",
  content = "docs",
  structure = "latest",
  send_cue = "always",
  send_strategy = "sync-purge",
  send_inspect = "none"
)

Local archive setup 

# Raw data to local archive
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "raw-data-archive",
  content = "raw-data",
  path = "~/research-archive/my-project/raw-data",
  structure = "archive",
  send_cue = "if-change",
  send_strategy = "sync-diff",
  send_inspect = "manifest"
)

# Output to network drive
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "output-network",
  content = "output",
  path = "/mnt/shared/project/output",
  structure = "latest",
  send_cue = "always",
  send_strategy = "sync-purge",
  send_inspect = "none"
)

Multiple remotes

projr uploads to every archive selected under build.dest during each production build.

# GitHub for public sharing
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "output-@version",
  content = "output",
  structure = "archive"
)

# Local for quick backup
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "output-local",
  content = "output",
  path = "~/backup/output",
  structure = "archive"
)

# Network for team access
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "output-network",
  content = "output",
  path = "/mnt/shared/output",
  structure = "latest"
)

Build Workflow

Production builds publish to the archives selected under build.dest and to any one-off archive requested in the call.

projr_build_dev()   # does NOT upload to remotes
projr_build_patch() # uploads (0.1.0 -> 0.1.1)
projr_build_minor() # uploads (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0)
projr_build_major() # uploads (0.1.0 -> 1.0.0)

Build steps with remotes configured:

  1. Clear output directories, run pre-build hooks, hash input files
  2. Bump version
  3. Render documents and scripts
  4. Hash output files, update manifest
  5. Git commit (if configured)
  6. Upload to remotes
  7. Run post-build hooks

Check and validate your configuration:

projr_yml_get()$remotes
projr_yml_check()

If a destination has no new files, check its configured labels and whether they changed during a production build. For GitHub, also check release write access.

Best Practices

  • Use a literal tag such as archive to keep several builds in one GitHub release. Use raw-data-@version when each build needs its own release.
  • Archive raw-data separately from output.
  • Start with the defaults: structure = "archive", send_strategy = "sync-diff", send_cue = "if-change", send_inspect = "manifest".
  • Use send_cue = "if-change" for large, rarely-changing datasets.
  • For local remotes, prefer absolute paths (~/archive/, /mnt/shared/).
  • Store tokens in _environment.local only – never commit secrets.
  • Test configuration with projr_build_dev() first (no uploads).
  • For slow uploads, switch to "sync-diff" + "manifest" inspection.

Quick Reference 

# Minimal GitHub remote
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "output-@version",
  content = "output"
)

# Minimal local remote
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "output-backup",
  content = "output",
  path = "~/archive/output"
)

# Run production build
projr_build_patch()

Recommended defaults:

Parameter Default Purpose
structure "archive" Version tracking
send_cue "if-change" Skip unchanged content
send_strategy "sync-diff" Transfer only differences
send_inspect "manifest" Fast remote inspection
